boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Kolb's Farm record (June 22, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. Cox calls the action the affair at Culp's farm. It falls inside the Marietta aggregate (GA013), which does not repeat its figures. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields read Two corps [US] and Hood s Corps [CS] without counts; the live field reads zero. Cox says Hood attacked with his whole corps, Hindman's and Stevenson's divisions in front and Stewart in support, and that Hooker reported, from prisoners' second-hand information, being attacked by three corps. Hood's report of that night says Stevenson's division was mainly engaged and Hindman's slightly. Cox writes that, in the style of Confederate reports, one could say Hood's corps attacked two brigades and was defeated, but argues that the whole force within supporting distance on each side should be counted.
claims.rationale: Formation statements that conflict in scope; no count is inspected and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Cox says the repulse was complete and the Confederates retreated to their entrenchments. Hood's report that night says he drove the enemy back, taking one line of breastworks and part of a second, and his corps report says the divisions drove the enemy from two lines of works. NPS says Sherman's envelopment had momentarily failed.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Hood's account of taking works conflicts with Cox and the frozen result.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 1,350 (US 350; CS 1,000). Cox says Johnston admitted a loss of about a thousand, that Williams reported 130, Geary's loss was trifling and Hascall's about the same as Williams's, and that nearly sixty Confederate dead lay before Gallup's regiment. Hood's note gives no totals.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Cox's Union components are partial; the frozen Union 350 has no inspected basis.

open_questions: Hooker's, Williams's, Geary's, Schofield's and Hascall's reports, Stevenson's and Hindman's division reports, Johnston's report (not a family here) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Hood's June 22, 1864 note and corps report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, are a third family (interested Confederate accounts). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
